name: Orbit AI - Phase 3 - Load Campaign hopper (W3.2)

nodes.name: Load campaign webhook
nodes.notes: REDEFINED this pass from the original catalog's 'Per-user isolated queue assignment' - that description contradicted the confirmed design (no multi-member campaign, a shared pool by default). This workflow is what actually loads a batch of Opportunities into a Campaign's hopper as queueable HopperEntry rows - see CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's Campaign/HopperEntry objects. Input contract: {campaignName, source, opportunityIds: string[]} - source is e.g. a scraper batch ID or niche selection, matching the brief's 'on-demand niche scraping' / 'dialer hopper async scrape' framing (05 Section 1/4).

nodes.name: Create Campaign
nodes.notes: No membership/ownership set here on purpose - a Campaign is not gated to specific reps, confirmed explicitly ('no multi-member campaign'). Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every workflow in this library.

nodes.name: Respond: campaign created

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, campaignId: $json.id, opportunityIdsRequested: $('Load campaign webhook').item.json.body.opportunityIds.length }) }}

nodes.notes: Responds as soon as the Campaign itself exists, not after every HopperEntry is created - the entry-creation loop (below) is fire-and-forget relative to this response, same reasoning as W1.6's Location-status-update branch: the caller doesn't need to block on N individual writes, and a partial failure there surfaces via this workflow's errorWorkflow alert, not a failed HTTP response. Field renamed from 'entriesQueued' to 'opportunityIdsRequested' this pass - now that a TCPA-consent check (below) can exclude some requested IDs from actually being queued, reporting a count synchronously here would either be wrong (claiming all were queued before the async consent checks even run) or require blocking on them, defeating the fire-and-forget design. The real queued count is only knowable by querying HopperEntries for this campaignId after the fact.

nodes.name: Split opportunityIds
nodes.notes: Splits the webhook payload's opportunityIds array into one item per Opportunity to queue. Reads directly off the trigger node's own output (no upstream transform needed) since Create Campaign's response doesn't carry this array.

nodes.name: Fetch Opportunity (TCPA check)
nodes.notes: 05 Section 1: 'TCPA consent capture - recorded at entry; no consent = excluded from auto-dial.' Every Opportunity queued into an auto-dial campaign hopper gets checked here first - lead-intake-to-demo-dashboard.workflow.json (W1.1) is what actually records tcpaConsent, this is where the exclusion rule gets enforced.

nodes.name: Has TCPA consent?
nodes.notes: Fails closed: anything other than an explicit true (missing field, false, null) excludes the record - 'no consent = excluded,' not 'assume consent unless explicitly declined.' Excluded Opportunities are just never queued (no HopperEntry created) - a quiet skip by design, not an error, since 'this lead can't be auto-dialed yet' is an expected, common outcome, not a failure worth alerting on for every occurrence.

nodes.name: Create HopperEntry

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ campaignId: $('Create Campaign').item.json.id, opportunityId: $('Split opportunityIds').item.json.body.opportunityIds, status: 'Available', attemptCountThisWave: 0, wave: 1 }) }}

nodes.notes: Runs once per split item - 'body.opportunityIds' on the split item is the single opportunity ID for this iteration (n8n's Split Out node keeps the same field name for the individual value, per the same pattern already used elsewhere in this library). Every entry starts wave 1, zero attempts, Available (unclaimed, in the shared pool).
